chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Umayyah (Aban ibn Uthman), from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man is given the zakat, and he distributes it among his companions; can he take something from it (for himself)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.
ai.seo_question: Can a person who receives zakat to distribute among others keep a portion for themselves?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of a zakat recipient who acts as a distributor, affirming that he may retain a portion for his own personal use even if he is among those receiving the funds. This ruling underscores the principle that zakat ownership transfers to the recipient upon delivery, allowing them discretion over their share, a key point in Shia fiqh regarding the distribution of alms. It resolves potential confusion about whether a recipient must pass on their entire share if they are also involved in the distribution process.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Saeed Bin Yasaar who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The man is given the Zakāt to distribute it among his companions. Can he take anything from it (for himself)?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Sa‘id ibn Yasar who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man to whom Zakat is given for distribution, if he can take a certain amount for himself. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, can do so.’”
